# Handwritten database contract

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — X1 adds typed observation subjects to the 25
> Step 0 relations; F1 validates their identity and scope, while E2a remains the
> metadata producer slice.

## Purpose and ownership

`schema/contract.json` owns the version-one relation inventory, column types,
primary keys, enums and serialization encodings. `schema/abi.py` supplies
reference encoders and validates unordered fact collections. Its `dbscheme()`
renders the committed `schema/evaluation.dbscheme`; the ABI check rejects
divergence. All 25 handwritten relations are independent of generated AST entity
types, so later syntax and evaluation producers can contribute to one database
without manufacturing raw kit labels.

F0 proves the prerequisites in [integration-gate.md](integration-gate.md). F1
defines the shared ABI; later producers and QL consumers preserve it rather than
infer semantics from missing rows.

## Durable identity

Global keys use `nixql:v1:<namespace>:` followed by
`<UTF-8-byte-length>:<component>` for each component. Namespace and component
boundaries distinguish equal-looking concatenations; empty components remain
present. No Unicode normalization, path resolution or worktree-prefix insertion
occurs in this encoder.

The frozen semantic components are:

- Root: logical name and root content identity.
- File: root key, root-relative path and file content digest. Absolute checkout
  locations are mapping data.
- Anchor: file key, decimal start byte, exclusive end byte, grammar kind and
  canonical ordered structural child-index path. Equal spans with different
  kinds or child paths remain distinct.
- Evaluation fingerprint: evaluator, lib, adapter and model versions;
  manifest-arguments hash; source-snapshot hash; policy hash; and system.
  Context, option-path segments, observation facet and occurrence distinctions
  must survive in the identities built on that fingerprint.

The validator reconstructs file and anchor keys and checks their components.
Other entity keys are checked for namespace and framing, not reconstructed from
their semantic inputs. The component list freezes the producer obligation;
accepting a well-framed target key is not evidence that its fingerprint was
computed correctly.

Option/request paths are compact canonical JSON arrays of exact string segments:
`["a.b"]` differs from `["a","b"]`. Contexts are root-only with instance path
`[]`; structural child paths contain nonnegative integer indexes. Canonical JSON
uses UTF-8 text, no optional whitespace and no ASCII-only escaping. Source paths
must be nonempty, relative and free of `..` segments; this lexical check does
not resolve symlinks or authenticate filesystem contents.

## Priority and exact text

Native relation integers are nonnegative and at most `2147483647`, rejecting
Python Booleans. Enum columns accept only the listed contract values. Unknown
optional information belongs in an absent auxiliary relation, rather than an
invented enum value or default false.

Option priority holds canonical signed decimal text over
`[-9223372036854775808,9223372036854775807]`. Zero is `0`; a nonzero magnitude
has no leading zero, plus sign or exponent. Negative override priorities are
valid. Consumers must retain decimal precision rather than narrow priorities to
a native QL integer. `priority-domain-unsupported` identifies an unsupported
range. An option priority also requires same-option `isDefined = true` metadata
and an observed `pre-apply-metadata` witness from an `option-metadata` request
with facet `priority`, the exact option path and context, and a `complete` or
`partial` result. Step 0 observations use only the `pre-apply-metadata` stage
and requests use only the `option-metadata` domain. The sole option metadata
field is `isDefined`.

Every text column is limited to **1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes**, measured before TRAP
quote doubling. JSON payloads and path arrays are checked after JSON encoding,
including escaping expansion. Invalid UTF-8 and oversized fields raise
`ValueError`; no truncation or chunk protocol exists. Global key framing itself
is exempt; keys repeated in text columns still obey the ceiling.

A later producer must reject an oversized file/projection transaction and report
`text-field-too-large` using representable enclosing identities. It must publish
no clipped facts or successful observations from that transaction. F1 validates
facts supplied to it; it does not implement atomic publication, automatically
manufacture failure rows or preflight the generated syntax writer. F0 documents
the pinned kit's separate preflight evidence.

## Scope, admission and completeness

Primary keys are unique per relation, definition ordinals are unique per option,
foreign entities must exist with the declared type. `nx_observations` contains
only observation, request, stage and state. Every observation in every state has
exactly one subject row in total: `nx_observation_options(observation, option)`
or `nx_observation_definitions(observation, definition)`. Both columns are typed
entity references; text subject kind/key columns are removed. Missing,
duplicate, wrong-type, dangling and simultaneous option/definition links are
invalid.

Requests belong to their context's target. The linked option, or a linked
definition's parent option, must belong to that exact context and hence target.
A request path need not equal its subject's option path except for the priority
witness above. Consumers must join typed subjects, rather than infer identity
from request paths or metadata presence. A definition observation identifies
only its linked definition, not every sibling definition of its option.

`nx_target_inputs` admits a file to the source snapshot of its target's run. For
origins used by declarations or definitions, an `nx_origin_files` link must have
admission for every referencing run's snapshot. Admission is supplied evidence:
F1 neither hashes source bytes nor authenticates labels, roots or symlink
policy. Diagnostics link directly to requests and targets; no diagnostic-origin
relation is retained. File-level links do not establish expression-to-value
edges or unique syntax associations.

Every `observed` observation requires its own `complete` or `partial` request
result. Missing rows mean unknown. Completed definitions require positive work
and contiguous ordinals for the request's same-path/context observed options.

A complete request cannot carry a timeout/text refusal reason or a linked
diagnostic with either code. Failed discovery can be represented before any
target exists. The validator checks these recorded consistency rules; it does
not prove that all phases/results were reported, that a budget was obeyed, that
a completion claim is true, or that all unobserved facts are false.

## Validation and changes

`checks/fixtures/abi/golden.py` supplies independent serialization expectations
and a graph covering every relation. `test_abi.py` checks identity,
enum/reference/scope rules, priority witnesses, refusal and UTF-8/JSON-expansion
boundaries. `checks/abi.nix` runs these tests, checks schema projection
equality, compiles against the standalone handwritten schema and imports/checks
typed golden TRAP. This does not prove production extraction.

Change the contract first, update validation and independent ABI/F2/supervisor
fixtures, regenerate `evaluation.dbscheme` through `dbscheme()` and the combined
schema through S1, then format affected files. Run the owner ABI, contracts, raw
inventory and evaluation-isolation checks through CI. Preserve typed-schema
import coverage, scope rejection tests and adversarial subject-link controls. An
ABI change requires full database regeneration; version one promises no in-place
upgrade or migration path.

## Deferred consumers

Increment 3 restores context-parent/module graph tables, definition-order
priorities, nested contexts and their scope validators and native Boolean
encoding. Increment 4 restores value/scalar/member/string-context tables,
encodings, value observations and their validators. Additional option metadata
fields return with their named consuming query; schema contexts are dropped
because increment 3 selects concrete instances only. The diagnostic-origin
relation is permanently dropped. These surfaces have no Step 0 producer or
consumer.

# Evaluation isolation and projection publication

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — E1 implements the serialized projection
> boundary; E2a adds [module metadata](module-adapter.md).

## Purpose and fit

`src/eval/supervisor.py` accepts an F2 manifest, explicit opaque-reference
bindings and a TRAP destination through `supervise`. It launches one subprocess
at a time for each selected request. Failure in one request leaves completed
projections available. It does not discover flake outputs, enter a devenv shell
or select an adapter from its label. E2a reports module-adapter support. The F2
`option-metadata` domain supports `declarations`, `definitions`, `isDefined` and
`priority` facets at root depth (`maxDepth = 0`) in `metadata` mode.

`src/eval/protocol.py` enables all three F2 custom formats and delegates exact
text, identity and fact validation to F1's `schema/abi.py`. Its TRAP renderer
uses F1 global labels and columns. Keep this shared authority: adding a second
relation validator or inferring success from empty output would violate the
[database](database-contract.md) and [target](target-contract.md) contracts.

## Runtime bindings and admission

The caller supplies a map resolving `evaluation.reference`, `moduleArgumentsRef`
and `specialArgumentsRef`; labels are never parsed as selectors. A binding
selects either an explicit `expression` path or a trusted fixture `command`.
Module and special arguments must be JSON representable. This boundary does not
transport arbitrary runtime functions or secret-bearing argument closures.

For a real expression, the supervisor resolves the path under a declared source
root, hashes each admitted root with Nix and imports a hash-pinned local
`fetchTree` copy. A separate admitted tree carries the request job. Roots are
admitted whole directories; this is not file-level snapshot authentication.
Descriptor identity and fingerprint strings are caller-supplied evidence, not
independently authenticated hashes of the copied roots.

A second declared root is accessible through its exact hash-pinned local
`fetchTree` URI. A projection may use this shape, with that root's actual path
and independently computed `nix hash path` result:

```nix
import ((builtins.fetchTree {
  narHash = "sha256-<root hash>";
  path = "/absolute/declared/dependency";
  type = "path";
}).outPath + "/value.nix")
```

Original absolute imports are not rewritten and remain blocked by pure
evaluation. E1 does not manufacture framework input handles. Each request gets a
disposable local Nix store and writable home/cache/temp directory. The
environment is rebuilt, and Nix receives pure/restricted evaluation, offline
operation, an allowlist of the exact pinned local tree URIs, no substitution, no
builders, `max-jobs = 0` and disabled import-from-derivation. No lock-update
command is invoked. These controls apply to Nix expression bindings; a trusted
command binding is a test transport and does not receive a network or filesystem
sandbox.

The Linux check supplies `pkgs.nix` (tested Nix 2.34.9) from the flake's locked
nixpkgs through `CODEQL_NIX_TEST_NIX`; production callers select the executable
through `supervise(..., nix=...)`. Changing that runtime requires rerunning the
real isolation cases. This slice makes no Darwin isolation claim.

## Budgets and transaction boundary

A request deadline covers root hashing and evaluation. Child processes get a new
process group, an address-space ceiling from `maxMemoryMiB` and disabled core
dumps. Both output pipes are drained, with their combined bytes bounded by
`maxBytes` (`byte-limit` on overflow). F1 separately enforces its per-field
1,048,576-byte ceiling (`text-field-too-large`); multiple legal fields may
exceed that size in aggregate. Timeout or excess output kills and reaps the
process group. Run diagnostics retain at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes of a message.

Accepted output must be one F2 envelope with exactly its request result. Options
and observations must match the selected context, path and request; metadata
must match the requested facet. Every observation has exactly one typed subject
link, validated by F1; the supervisor accepts option subjects for emitted
options and definition subjects for emitted definitions. A complete projection
observes each emitted option and definition exactly once. Origins belong to
emitted definitions or declarations, and positions belong to those origins.
Producers cannot emit supervisor facts. [E2a](module-adapter.md) authenticates
caller-admitted source links.

A complete request requires a positive observed count and an `observed` option
witness for the selected facet. `isDefined` and `priority` also require their
respective metadata rows; declarations may be empty with an observed option. F1
independently requires each priority's same-option `isDefined = true` and
priority-request observation. A result-only envelope, unforced observation or
missing metadata cannot establish success. The complete graph passes F1
validation before publication. `maxNodes` bounds option, definition,
declaration, observation and reported counts. Child limits exclude JSON/F1
validation and publication; the supervisor has no aggregate memory ceiling.

Each validated projection is written to a temporary file, flushed and renamed to
a completed `.trap` file. An invalid transaction publishes no metadata.
Supervisor-owned run, phase, target, context, capability, request and diagnostic
rows are published separately at completion. This is a per-projection handoff,
not an atomic whole-run snapshot or a proof of crash recovery. Completed
transactions survive another request's error. Strict mode raises
`ExtractionFailed` after publishing status evidence, carrying the full validated
packet.

Missing bindings, denied paths, missing inputs and recognized evaluator refusals
are blocked; other producer errors fail. Targets and the evaluation phase expose
incomplete requests. Exception messages classify some Nix refusals, so changed
runtime wording requires checking the blocked/failed distinction. A malformed
manifest records failed discovery before any target is admitted. Missing
observations never imply absent options or completed metadata.

## Exact CI entry point and cases

`checks.nix` imports `checks/eval-isolation.nix`, exposing the Linux-only
`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-eval-isolation`. It runs
`checks/fixtures/eval-isolation/test_supervisor.py` through F3's explicit
nonempty domain runner. The runner reports each named test and its executed
count; `$out/evidence` is written only after the suite passes. No CodeQL engine
or database import runs in this check.

The fixture has two complementary oracle groups:

- Fake producers check bound arguments, literal target names and paths, statuses
  and completed-file handoff; serialized execution; error isolation with
  strict-mode evidence; crash/malformed/invalid/forged/foreign-request, context,
  option-path and origin refusal; time, address-space, output, root depth, node
  and diagnostic budgets; invalid manifests (including lone surrogates), custom
  formats and missing opaque bindings; unrequested metadata; legal multi-field
  output above 1 MiB versus aggregate/individual overflow; actual metadata
  record counts at and over the node budget despite a smaller reported count;
  refusal of result-only, unobserved or missing-metadata success; all three
  metadata facets and priority's independent witness.
- Real Nix checks compare `isDefined` metadata to an independently invoked
  direct Nix Boolean expression with an unselected throwing leaf; import an
  admitted sibling and bound arguments; read a second declared root through its
  pinned `fetchTree`; distinguish a selected throw from a missing input; hide a
  host environment input; deny an undeclared path and an expression outside the
  roots; refuse a hash-pinned loopback fetch before the HTTP server receives a
  request; and reject IFD without a builder marker or lockfile appearing.

These tests establish the exercised runtime controls and projection handoff.
They do not establish general adapter correctness, scalar/path serialization,
string contexts, authenticated source provenance, a production extractor or
queryable combined database. Those need their own slice checks.

## Changing the boundary

Keep F1/F2 authority and the owner-local check import. Add independent failure
and positive controls to the explicit fixture when changing binding admission,
subprocess handling, budgets, publication or evaluator flags. Preserve
successful unrelated requests and health evidence on failures. Format changed
files, run the affected owner checks, and update this note and the existing
registry source list when the abstraction changes. Regenerate instruction
projections through `generate:all`; never edit generated consumers directly.

## Deferred consumers

Increment 4 restores value/member/scalar/string-context validation and fixtures,
including selected-root value success, opaque/empty/null witnesses,
reachability, cycles, shared DAG processing and longest-path depth checks. Their
text and aggregate-output checks remain here on metadata rows. Increment 3
restores nested contexts; the retained transport accepts roots only. E2a
supplies the module adapter and admitted syntax-to-origin links without adding a
value serializer.

# Installed Nix extractor

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — P2a installs one coordinator for database
> creation and query tests, preserving authenticated partial work; Q0 adds a
> separate installed lifecycle check.

## Terms

- ABI: the shared database tables, identities and text encodings.
- Anchor: a syntax node identified by file, byte range, kind and child path.
- Binding: an explicit map entry resolving an evaluation or argument reference.
- Coordinator: the program that admits sources and joins both producers.
- Discovery: evaluating the project function that declares targets and bindings.
- Extractor: the installed program and schema CodeQL uses to build a database.
- NAR hash: Nix's content hash of a complete directory tree.
- Oracle: an expected answer obtained independently of extraction.
- Pack: a named CodeQL library, query or test directory.
- Producer: a component that emits syntax or evaluation facts.
- Q0: the Step 0 query about which file retains an option definition.
- QL: CodeQL's query language.
- Request: an explicit option path, metadata facet and work limits.
- Run: one extraction identity joining schema, implementation and source
  snapshot.
- Snapshot: admitted source identities, directory hashes and selected file
  digests.
- Target: an explicitly named configuration with bounded requests.
- TRAP: the fact-file format CodeQL imports.

## What installs and why

`lib/packaging.nix` assembles extractor, library and query products. The
extractor's schema and statistics are copied from the library, preserving one
schema for fact import and query compilation. Its `autobuild.sh`,
`index-files.sh` and `qltest.sh` hooks all invoke `src/extract.py` through the
same coordinator launcher. This keeps ordinary database creation and query tests
on the production path.

The recipes under `packages/ai/devTools/` expose the separate products and a
`codeql-nix` command. That command uses the existing CodeQL owner's
`customizePackage` interface to install the Nix extractor and packs beside its
engine. `lib/default.nix` exposes the same packaging function. Pack identities
remain those established by [owner-layout.md](owner-layout.md); the library
retains its own location interface.

## Admission and discovery

Invoke the customized command with
`codeql database create --language=nix --source-root=PROJECT DATABASE`. The
`inputs` extractor option is a JSON map from input name to `{path, narHash}`;
each path must be an absolute directory and match its supplied NAR hash. The
coordinator first copies the project into a private directory and hashes that
stable copy. It excludes only exact CodeQL work-in-progress database, TRAP,
archive and scratch paths supplied by the engine, so query-test output under the
source root cannot change the admitted bytes. Query tests supply the same input
map through `CODEQL_EXTRACTOR_NIX_OPTION_INPUTS`.

The default target file is `.nixql/targets.nix` under the source root. The
`targets` extractor option selects another admitted file; relative paths resolve
under that root. Its `{ inputs, source }: { manifest, bindings }` function
receives pinned local input trees and project source. Discovery uses the
existing evaluation supervisor's offline, restricted, pure Nix invocation and
process controls, with a 60-second deadline, 2048 MiB memory limit and 8 MiB
output limit. Discovery passes its initial directory hashes through
`sourcePins`; the evaluator must match them before constructing pinned local
input trees. Coordinated evaluation requests enforce the same guard. No second
discovery evaluator is introduced.

The result must contain exactly `manifest` and `bindings`, with the manifest
passing the existing [target contract](target-contract.md). Returned copied-tree
paths are restored to admitted paths before request processing; project
evaluation uses the private copy. Syntax retains the original project path for
file and archive identity, checks those bytes against the copied-file digests
and snapshots each file for parsing. Target source roots must match admitted
directory paths. Their content identities and snapshot fingerprints are replaced
with the coordinator's admitted identities; caller labels do not determine the
installed run snapshot.

## One run across both producers

`RunIdentity` in `src/extract.py` owns the shared identity. It hashes the
installed combined schema, producer implementation bytes, admitted root
identities and selected file digests. Named dependency pins participate even
though their syntax is not selected. Only project-root `*.nix` files are
selected for syntax extraction.

The coordinator passes that identity to [syntax extraction](source-identity.md)
and the [evaluation supervisor](evaluation-isolation.md). Syntax checks its
manifest snapshot; evaluation checks target snapshot fingerprints. Each returned
fact collection must pass ABI validation and contain exactly the expected run
row. A foreign run or snapshot is refused. Coordinated children omit their run
row when writing TRAP; the coordinator publishes the sole `nx_runs` row. The
syntax module loads the neighboring coordinator by file path, preserving
callers' module search paths when imported as a standalone driver.

Syntax and evaluation write into temporary staging directories. Authenticated
file rows and copied-path mappings connect evaluation origins through the
existing [module adapter](module-adapter.md). The supervisor admits
authenticated selected files by exact target root name and content identity
before evaluation, preserving candidates after failed work. Copied-path mappings
retain all file identities; links require exactly one in the target admission
plus trusted provenance and matching original/copied bytes. Explicit labels and
ambiguous aliases leave origins unlinked. Before copying staged archives and
TRAP into CodeQL's destinations, the coordinator validates the combined facts,
recopies the original project with the same exclusions and checks its NAR hash
against the initial private copy. It also rehashes admitted dependencies. A
changed snapshot refuses staged publication, including completed requests from
an otherwise partial run.

Publication copies completed files individually and writes the coordinator run
record afterward. This is no whole-run atomic rename or crash-recovery protocol.
Authenticated partial evaluation preserves completed request facts, per-request
failures and diagnostics, then returns nonzero when a phase is incomplete. Mixed
snapshots or invalid child facts never reach that promotion step. Missing,
throwing, malformed or forbidden-fetch discovery returns failure with a failed
phase and bounded diagnostic. Absent metadata never establishes success.

## Evidence and changes

`checks.nix` imports `checks/installed.nix`, exposing the Linux-only
`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-installed`. Its explicit nonempty runner
executes six installed-path tests and four separate review-regression tests
before writing `$out/evidence`. The installed tests cover offline language/pack
lookup, identical schema bytes, database creation with syntax and real module
metadata under one run, an explicit target file, query-test extraction,
discovery refusals and stale input pins. Direct Nix evaluation independently
checks priority changing from `100` to `50`. Q0 adds the query-level comparison
and failure cases in its separate [Step 0 check](step0-query.md); that check
must pass before claiming the installed Q0 acceptance contract.

The regression suite uses deterministic pin controls for a transient dependency
change during discovery, preservation of completed requests beside failed
requests, refusal to publish partial work after a snapshot change and standalone
syntax-module import. These checks exercise coordinator boundaries with
controlled producers, complementing the installed database tests.

The one-run and stale-pin cases do not independently inject a foreign child
envelope. Keep that distinction when reporting mixed-snapshot coverage. General
evaluator isolation and authenticated syntax mapping retain their separate owner
checks.

To change installation, edit the existing packaging assembly and recipes
together; keep all hooks on the coordinator and preserve shared schema bytes. To
change identity or admission, update `RunIdentity` and both producer boundaries
together, retaining ABI/target-contract validation and independent refusal
expectations. Register new fixtures through the owner check entry point. Format
changed files, run the affected owner checks through CI and update this note
plus its registry entry when these obligations change. Regenerate instruction
projections from their sources rather than editing generated consumers.

# Nix language integration gate

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — F0 shares pinned kit inputs and the canonical
> location adapter with S1; its bootstrap proof remains test-only.

## Purpose and boundary

F0 is a disposable fixture in `checks/fixtures/bootstrap/`, exposed by
`checks/bootstrap.nix` as `checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-bootstrap`. It settles
whether the shared tree-sitter kit, a handwritten relation and the existing
CodeQL engine can form one queryable database. It is not the production
extractor or an implementation of Nix evaluation: its second producer reads
`targets.tsv`.

The check uses `packages/codeql`'s existing JavaScript engine bundle. It builds
Rust with `rustPlatform.buildRustPackage` and vendored dependencies, generates
the syntax schema and `Ast.qll`, then appends `nx_bootstrap_targets`. No second
engine factory, discovery framework or configuration wrapper is introduced. The
result contains only an evidence file; the engine and trial databases remain
build inputs and temporary artifacts.

## Compatibility pins

- CodeQL CLI: `2.27.3`, checked against the existing owner's `sources.json` and
  asserted at execution.
- Grammar: `nix-community/tree-sitter-nix` commit
  `38a15330421d20f3a4d380759f9634d39ba3d8ec`; crate `0.3.0`.
- Kit: `github/codeql` tag `codeql-cli/v2.27.3`, commit
  `a1575b98a8cc19bcfa7bb6cb41be688cb3dae65c`; crate `codeql-extractor` `0.2.0`.
- Parser runtime: `tree-sitter` `0.26.13` in the committed `Cargo.lock`.

The fixed-output source hashes and Cargo vendor hash live in `lib/kit.nix`,
shared by F0 and S1; the bootstrap fixture's `Cargo.lock` fixes transitive
dependencies. Changing the CLI requires a kit compatibility audit rather than
silently keeping this proof valid.

## Installed interfaces and join

The installed extractor has `codeql-extractor.yml`, `nix.dbscheme`, its
same-basename statistics file and `tools/{autobuild,index-files,qltest}.sh`. The
descriptor selects `column_kind: utf8`, build mode `none` and the legacy test
hook. The separate library has its own manifest, generated schema, statistics,
generated syntax and handwritten QL.

`index-files.sh` receives a file-list path and emits syntax TRAP plus source
archives. The test hook indexes `.nix` files in the current fixture directory,
then separately launches the target producer into the same TRAP directory. Both
producers publish completed files by rename before the CLI imports the database.

`ql/lib/codeql/Locations.qll` is the canonical `overlay[local]` language
interface, copied into F0 by `checks/bootstrap.nix` and shared with S1: `File`
exposes absolute and source-root-relative paths; `Location` exposes its file and
start/end line/column. The generated syntax imports that interface.
Same-basename statistics belong beside the library schema as well as beside the
extractor schema.

`Bootstrap.qll` joins the handwritten target to a generated token through the
shared `@file` identity and exact token text, then returns its location. It does
not reconstruct a raw node label from coordinates. `Raw.ql` requires six
integer-token rows, including identical `41` text in two different files and a
recovered parse. `Join.ql` requires only `selected/41` and `coordinate/73`;
wrong-text, absent-file and unselected-file controls cannot join.

## Coordinates: measured and remaining

The six golden rows verify one-based, inclusive byte columns for integer tokens.
`coordinates.nix.in` becomes CRLF during the check; its second line contains a
tab and UTF-8 `é` before `73`. That token occupies columns 27–28, rather than
decoded-character columns 26–27. The third-line `97` occupies 10–11. A missing
right-hand side in `recovered.nix.in` still permits the subsequent `41` at line
3, columns 10–11.

These assertions establish this file/location interface and these token spans.
They do not establish a unique syntax anchor, Nix evaluator position conversion
or complete coordinate coverage. S2 still needs the companion anchor bridge and
tests for empty spans, identical/ambiguous spans, multiline end-at-line-start
conversion, comments, interpolation and paths. The pinned kit's
`extractor/mod.rs:955–1022` handles empty ranges and ends at a new line; that
source behavior is not independently asserted by these golden rows.

## Exact text before the kit can clip it

The pinned kit's `trap.rs:177–187` clips a string argument beyond 1,048,576
UTF-8 bytes before doubling quotes. `src/lib.rs` therefore checks converted
token text and normalized file/folder paths before real extraction. The selected
simple extraction path emits source text only through token values; grammar
product tables carry labels and integers. Empty-file and diagnostic-tag strings
are constants. The unused alternate parser path, YAML, database metadata and
overlays are outside this fixture's producers; the CLI supplies the source-root
prefix.

Raw TRAP diagnostic messages also contain the source path. A source-derived
bound covers the selected tuple diagnostic templates and grammar/schema names.
The kit's location-correction internal errors go only to its logger, not to the
`diagnostics` tuple. When that bound cannot guarantee a safe message, extraction
first applies path preflight and checks the diagnostic bound for a short virtual
path before invoking the kit privately at that path. This guarantees the dry
output has not been clipped. It then checks the actual decoded diagnostic
arguments with the real path restored before real extraction. This applies to
ordinary trees as well as recovered trees. The second producer checks each TSV
field and every normalized derived absolute file/folder path before publishing
its transaction.

The shared `syntax` function serves the installed extractor and
`bootstrap-probe`. The latter reads a synthetic absolute path from a UTF-8 file
and never creates or archives a file at that path. In probe mode, oversized
syntax fields return exit 2 with bounded `text-field-too-large` stderr and no
completed TRAP; oversized evaluation paths fail without publishing even an
earlier valid target.

`test-preflight.py` checks 18 token/path cases: attribute keys, quote-heavy
comments, virtual file paths, source path fragments, ASCII strings and multibyte
strings, each at 1,048,575, 1,048,576 and 1,048,577 bytes. Accepted arguments
must round-trip through decoded real TRAP tuples; oversized arguments must
visibly refuse. Ten more cases cover parse-error and ordinary-tree type-mismatch
diagnostics, including safe near-limit messages and oversized messages/paths.
Three evaluation cases independently size the derived absolute path at the same
boundaries, with every input TSV field individually within the limit. These 31
cases support the audited emission paths; they do not replace re-auditing the
selected schema and kit when either pin changes.

## Offline verification and maintenance

The Nix sandbox successfully resolves the installed extractor and runs
`codeql test run` against the separate local library: `Raw.ql` and `Join.ql`
both pass. With an empty search path, extractor lookup fails with no extractor
named `nix`; query compilation fails because `nix-agentic-tools/nix-bootstrap`
is not local and no dependency lock is present. The check requires both
failures. It does not attempt a dependency download or prove a general network
fallback policy. Rust compilation uses the Nix-vendored Cargo inputs offline;
initial admission of missing inputs is a separate operation.

Change this gate through its owner-local check and fixture, keeping
hand-authored expected rows independent of extractor output. Run the bootstrap
check after changing pins, schema assembly, installed entry points, path
handling or preflight. Re-audit all tuple-string emission sites, diagnostic
templates and UTF-8 conversion before claiming the changed kit preserves exact
text. Keep production schema/identity, adapters, anchors and evaluation status
machinery in their later slices; this fixture proves only their integration
prerequisites.

# Observed metadata library

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — L0 reads existing metadata and syntax facts.

- QL is the language for querying a CodeQL database.
- A target is an explicitly named configuration.
- A context is a target's root instance.
- A request selects an option path, metadata facet and work limits.
- An observation records an outcome for one typed option or definition.
- Selected means retained for type merging, without proving a value's cause.
- An origin is an evaluator label with an optional admitted file or point.
- An anchor identifies syntax by file, byte range, kind and child path.
- A candidate is a literal source binding matching an origin and option path.
- Association quality: zero candidates unmapped, one unique, many ambiguous.
- Priority is the override number, retained as exact signed decimal text.
- TRAP is the fact format imported into a CodeQL database.

`Targets.qll`, `Modules.qll` and `Origin.qll` expose only `Target`,
`RequestResult`, `ObservedOption`, `SelectedDefinition` and `Origin`. Private
`internal/Evaluation.qll` shares observation witnesses and path encoding over
the [existing tables](database-contract.md). Request results retain failures.

Observed options require their typed subject link and an observed outcome from a
complete or partial request. Selected definitions require their own such link
and an observed parent option; request paths and siblings cannot supply it.
Paths retain exact segments and target identity. Missing priority stays absent;
failed or missing observations establish neither selection nor a losing
definition.

Origins expose optional file paths and reported UTF-8 byte points. Candidates
reuse [authenticated anchors](source-identity.md), require target admission and
match exact literal paths. Association quality cannot identify the expression
that produced a value. Equal-priority definitions may all remain selected.

The owner's `checks.nix` imports `checks/metadata.nix`, which runs handwritten
`ql/test/step0/Metadata.ql` expectations over independently assembled TRAP.
Cases cover failed/missing work, typed subjects, sparse definition observations,
exact paths, distinct targets, signed endpoints and origin association controls.
Live evaluation needs separate proof. Update accessors and expectations
together; format changes and run `codeql-nix-metadata` through CI.

# Module metadata adapter

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — E2a emits root option metadata with X1 typed
> observation subjects; native paths retain provenance and selected syntax
> admission is independent of retained origins.

An adapter obtains configuration plus option metadata: a rich result.
`src/eval/nix/adapters/evalModules.nix` takes pinned `lib`, module paths and
JSON arguments; `src/eval/nix/modules.nix` selects one option's metadata without
values. Definitions are retained assignments; declarations introduce options;
origins are file labels; priority is the override number, lower wins. Tied
definitions survive. Every emitted option and retained definition has its own
observation and exactly one typed `nx_observation_options` or
`nx_observation_definitions` link; definition observations identify their
sibling ordinal through the definition entity, never through request text.
`definitions` adds contiguous ordinals beside `declarations`, `isDefined` and
`priority`; priority includes `isDefined`. The
[supervisor](evaluation-isolation.md) keeps limits and publication. Callers
supply [S2](source-identity.md) file rows and copy mappings; original and copied
bytes must match before linking. Implicit native module paths retain Nix string
context without changing their label spelling. Plain absolute strings, synthetic
labels, explicit `_file` and explicit definition labels prove no source
identity. The supervisor admits selected authenticated syntax files by exact
target root name and content identity before requests run; unselected files and
failed requests retain this admission. Origin-file links still require trusted
labels plus matching original and copied bytes. Missing rows mean unknown.
Re-audit lazy label normalization before value consumers. Change these producers
together, preserving F1 validation and F2 authorization. Run
`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-modules` for direct Nix comparisons and
refusals; format edits and regenerate through `generate:all`.

# Nix CodeQL owner and test entry points

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — Step 0 retains 25 metadata relations and
> explicit owner check imports; document and check inventories live in the owner
> registry and checks entry point. S1 adds combined-schema generation and
> standalone raw location tests; E1 adds the isolated metadata projection check;
> S2 registers source and anchor acceptance; Q0 adds the installed query check.

## Purpose and fit

`packages/codeql-nix/` owns the Nix language contracts, fixtures and pack
manifests. Its `registry.nix` is the source of scoped architecture documents,
including this note. It contributes through the existing owner registry; no root
owner allowlist or separate discovery mechanism is needed.

`checks.nix` is the source of explicit check imports. Supporting files are not
recursively discovered as checks. Each imported check declares its selected
fixtures, dependencies and platform guards. Add a deliberate owner-local import
when adding a domain, without changing the root flake or copying the inventory
into this document.

## Checks and nonempty evidence

The bootstrap proves its disposable syntax/target integration fixture. The ABI
check validates the handwritten schema and independent typed golden TRAP. The
contracts check runs explicitly selected Python suites, including the
manifest/observation boundary, runner behavior and ABI/health sentinels. These
fixture checks do not establish production extraction. Read their imports and
commands through `checks.nix` for the current check and suite inventory.

A check must fail when a selected suite fails and publish its evidence only
after every selected suite passes. Register transport tests in an owner check so
verification does not depend on a manual invocation.

`checks/run-domain-tests.py` accepts one or more explicit unittest file paths.
Each file runs in a separate Python process, with its parent directory available
for companion imports. The runner reports total and executed test counts per
file. Missing files, import errors, failed tests, empty suites, entirely skipped
suites and early `SystemExit` fail the aggregate. It never searches sibling
directories for tests; a passing suite cannot hide an empty later suite.

The ABI sentinel validates the golden graph and compares its relation inventory
with an independently spelled set of all 25 Step 0 relations. The health
sentinel requires runs, targets, syntax results and request results, completed
discovery, successful target/syntax statuses and positive request work counts.
These witnesses prevent empty or failed fixture output from looking like clean
analysis. They validate the fixture contract, not live extraction health or
future evaluator completeness.

`codeql-nix-eval-isolation` adds the Linux-only E1 supervisor fixture through
the same domain runner. Its fake producers and real minimal Nix projections
check serialized metadata requests, budgets, refusal paths and validated TRAP
handoff. See [evaluation-isolation.md](evaluation-isolation.md) for admission
rules, runtime limits and the exact cases. This check supplies no module adapter
or CodeQL database import.

## Pack boundaries

Each pack has its own `qlpack.yml` at the reserved interface:

- `ql/lib/`: `nix-agentic-tools/nix-all`, a library selecting `nix.dbscheme` and
  extractor `nix`.
- `ql/queries/`: `nix-agentic-tools/nix-queries`, depending on `nix-all`.
- `ql/test/`: `nix-agentic-tools/nix-tests`, depending on `nix-all` and
  selecting extractor `nix`.

All versions are `0.0.0`; these manifests establish identities. The
[installed extractor](installed-extractor.md) assembles the installed products.
`ql/lib/nix.dbscheme` is a symlink to `../../generated/nix.dbscheme`, S1's
combined generated/handwritten schema. S1's private raw QL and location adapter
supply the library's syntax interface; `codeql-nix-raw-inventory` checks
deterministic generation, inventory drift and standalone generated-node
file/location traversal. S2 adds the syntax driver and private
[authenticated anchor bridge](source-identity.md), tested by
`codeql-nix-anchors` through F3 driver contracts, raw preflight and QL/archive
assertions. The installed extractor, public metadata API and
[Step 0 queries](step0-query.md) now have separate owner checks; Q0 acceptance
requires its installed lifecycle check to pass. The bootstrap's separate fixture
packs remain disposable evidence.

## Adding a domain

Reserve a distinct `ql/test/<domain>/` for each domain's source, `.ql` and
reviewed `.expected` fixtures, and a distinct `checks/fixtures/<domain>/` when
Python or other contract fixtures are needed. Keep those paths disjoint from the
existing `abi`, `bootstrap`, `contracts`, `eval-isolation` and `protocol`
fixtures. A directory reservation does not implement a later capability or make
it a passing test.

Add an owner-local `checks/<domain>.nix` and explicitly import it from
`checks.nix`. For Python contracts, invoke `checks/run-domain-tests.py` with the
exact selected files and declare their dependencies in that check. For QL
fixtures, a domain check must explicitly run the appropriate tests against its
required producer/library; the Python runner does not run CodeQL tests. Preserve
the nonempty guards and independent expectations rather than learning expected
output from the implementation.

Keep shared pack manifests and the ABI coordinated instead of letting domains
rewrite them independently. Change F1 first when relation semantics change;
update F2's independent transport fixtures when that boundary changes.
Production extractor installation needs its own checks before this note can
claim that capability. Format changed files with `treefmt`, run the affected
checks through CI and update this note when ownership or entry-point obligations
change.

# Source transactions and syntax anchors

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — S2 authenticates archived source bytes and
> transports the companion anchor index through the existing kit metadata table.

`lib/packaging.nix` exposes
`syntaxDriver/bin/nixql-syntax MANIFEST_JSON OUTPUT_DIRECTORY`. The manifest
supplies roots with `logicalName`, `rootContentIdentity`, `path`, `sourceKind`
and explicit `files` entries containing root-relative `path` and the SHA-256
`contentHash` of admitted bytes. This syntax-only input is separate from the
evaluation target manifest. F1's durable identities retain its existing
root/file/anchor components; SHA-256 authenticates this driver's snapshot
admission without changing the opaque digest ABI.

The driver resolves roots and source paths, refuses escapes through symlinks,
verifies the declared digest and snapshots the bytes privately. The pinned kit
and `src/anchors.rs` both read those snapshot bytes. A second checkout read
after extraction must match before publication. Byte edits change file and
anchor identity. `rootContentIdentity` is caller-supplied; the driver verifies
selected file digests rather than recomputing a digest of the whole root. Equal
text in different physical files remains distinct. Logical aliases of one
resolved path and digest reuse one raw parse and companion index while retaining
each file identity, anchor, metadata index and status. Every alias rechecks
containment and source bytes before cache reuse and publication; raw ambiguity
checks remain unchanged.

Completed raw TRAP is published by rename only after source authentication,
exact-text preflight and F1 transaction validation succeed. Source bytes are
archived under the absolute canonical path with its leading slash removed.
`CODEQL_EXTRACTOR_NIX_TRAP_DIR` and `CODEQL_EXTRACTOR_NIX_SOURCE_ARCHIVE_DIR`
select standard CodeQL publication destinations; otherwise `trap/` and
`archive/` live under the output directory. `facts.json` uses F2's envelope and
contains only F1 relations. Independent completed files survive a refusal. A
failed representable file retains its identity and failed syntax result, with a
bounded enclosing run diagnostic; oversized identity text retains only the
enclosing failure. Source publication is per file, not atomic across a run; the
archive entry is written before the completed TRAP file.

The companion index uses a line-start map over archived UTF-8 bytes. Columns
count bytes: tabs and CR each occupy one column. Raw ends are inclusive; a node
ending immediately after LF ends on the preceding line, including that LF's
column. Empty spans use the kit's start column minus one as the end column.
Anchors retain exclusive byte ends, original grammar kinds and ordered concrete
child-index paths. The index separately records the kit's structural path, which
excludes error/missing children from sibling ordinals and detaches extra tokens.
Pruned nodes retain anchors but have no precise raw association.

`nix/internal/RawBridge.qll` joins authenticated visible F1 identity components
to the raw `File` interface through namespaced `databaseMetadata` entries. It
checks grammar kind, normalized coordinates and the kit structural path before
counting raw candidates. One candidate is `unique`; zero is `unmapped`; multiple
are `ambiguous`. Only a unique association exposes a raw location. Raw labels
are never manufactured, shared with F1 entity types or exposed as durable
identity.

The private metadata keys frame root key, relative path and digest after a
namespaced prefix. `nixql.s2.file|` maps that identity to archived absolute path
and source byte length; `nixql.s2.line|` supplies one-based line numbers and
line-start byte offsets. `nixql.s2.path|` additionally keys the concrete child
path and supplies the kit structural path. Fields escape `%` as `%25` and `|` as
`%7C`, then join with `|`. RawBridge derives normalized coordinates from anchor
bytes and the independent line map; changing an anchor byte span cannot inherit
the original coordinates. Both metadata columns are exact UTF-8 tuple text and
are checked against F1's 1,048,576-byte ceiling before publication. These
entries use the existing generated schema table; S2 adds no handwritten ABI
relation or combined-schema table. They are not evaluation facts or
authenticated evaluator origins. As with every extractor relation, these are
trusted producer evidence; fabricating a file admission record is outside the QL
consumer's archive-authentication boundary. The driver tests establish that
boundary from actual bytes.

The raw writer reuses F0's audited token, path and diagnostic preflight before
calling the kit; added metadata and handwritten facts receive their own
preflight. An oversized field refuses the entire file transaction with
`text-field-too-large`, without raw nodes or anchors from that file. Re-audit
the raw writer when the grammar, kit or selected emission paths change.

`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-anchors` registers the driver suite through F3,
inherited raw preflight cases and independent QL/archive acceptance. Keep
expected rows independent of generated output, including duplicate raw
extraction, unauthenticated identities, Unicode/CRLF, empty spans and ends at a
line start. Later AST/evaluation slices must consume this bridge rather than
introduce a second source mapping.

To change this boundary, update the driver, companion index and RawBridge
together, keeping the metadata framing and concrete-to-kit path translation in
agreement. Change F1 first if durable identity or relation semantics change;
regenerate the combined schema through S1 when required. Format changed files
and run `checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-anchors` plus the affected ABI or
raw-inventory check. Keep archive and refusal controls: successful query rows
alone cannot establish that admitted bytes match the source snapshot.

# Target and observation contract

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — F2 retains the metadata manifest and fact
> envelope for Step 0; it implements no evaluator.

## Purpose and fit

`schema/target-manifest.json` describes explicit named targets and bounded
requests. `schema/observation-protocol.json` carries the resulting F1 facts.
Both use JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. These contracts let future producers and QL
consumers share fixtures before evaluation exists. The
[database contract](database-contract.md) remains authoritative for relation
semantics; the [integration gate](integration-gate.md) establishes only the
earlier bootstrap prerequisites.

## Explicit targets

Projects supply `.nixql/targets.nix`, a pure function receiving pinned inputs
and project source. Handles/arguments stay runtime-side; future E1 must bind
each opaque reference to its supplied handle/arguments without inferring from
labels. This JSON boundary specifies no binding-registry implementation and
transports no function or secret values.

The manifest is
`{ "manifestVersion": 1, "targets": { "stable.name": descriptor } }`. Names are
literal labels, never flake attribute selectors. Every descriptor requires:

- `adapter`, `adapterVersion` and explicit `system`.
- `argumentDescription`, containing `hash`, `moduleArgumentsRef` and
  `specialArgumentsRef`.
- `evaluation`, containing `kind` and opaque `reference`.
- `fingerprint`, containing `evaluatorVersion`, `libVersion`, `modelVersion`,
  `policyHash` and `sourceSnapshotHash`.
- Nonempty `inputIdentities` and `sourceRoots`.
- Nonempty `observationModes` and `requests`.
- Boolean `syntaxOnlyFallback`.

The adapter is `evalModules`; accepting a descriptor proves no adapter
implementation. Evaluation kinds are `arguments` and `rich-result`. References
identify admitted runtime handles or arguments; they do not serialize functions
or secrets wholesale. The argument-description hash records the admitted
description. `modelVersion` must be `not-requested` until increment 1 activates
generated model identities; the run's `modelHash` fixture uses the same
sentinel.

Input identities map exact input names to identity strings. Each source root has
`logicalName`, `path` and `rootContentIdentity`. Logical name and content
identity supply F1 root identity; checkout path is mapping data. The fingerprint
fields combine with `adapterVersion`, the argument-description hash and `system`
to supply F1 evaluation-fingerprint components. Validation checks their
representation, not their derivation, source admission, hash authenticity or
runtime-reference resolution.

## Requests and authorization

Every request explicitly provides `domain`, `facet`, literal string-segment
`path`, and all five budgets: `maxBytes`, `maxDepth`, `maxMemoryMiB`, `maxNodes`
and `maxSeconds`. `["a.b"]` and `["a", "b"]` remain distinct. There is no
implicit traversal or value request. The metadata baseline explicitly selects a
prefix.

Every request uses the `option-metadata` domain and `metadata` observation mode.
Facets: `declarations`, `definitions`, `isDefined`, `priority`. Objects are
closed to unknown fields; target and input maps permit explicit names.

Deferred surfaces return with their consuming queries: increment 3 restores
module graph requests and metadata enumeration; increment 4 restores
selected-value/member/string-context modes and scalar fixtures; increment 5
restores framework adapters, config-only handles and schema requests. Other
metadata facets return with the increment 3 module queries that consume them.
The `reusable` cache control returns in increment 8. Explicit input, argument,
root, system and fingerprint identities remain required now.

## Mandatory validation layers

Consumers must register and enable all three custom formats. A validator that
ignores formats does not enforce this contract:

- `nixql-exact-text`: a string must encode as UTF-8 and occupy at most 1,048,576
  bytes. Character count alone is insufficient.
- `nixql-native-int`: budgets must be native integers in `0..2147483647`,
  excluding Booleans and floats. Parsed JSON `1.0` is rejected even though
  ordinary JSON Schema `integer` accepts it; consumers must retain this
  distinction while decoding.
- `nixql-path`: a path must contain exact string segments, and its compact JSON
  serialization with `ensure_ascii=False` must fit the same UTF-8 byte ceiling,
  including brackets, quotes and escaping.

`checks/fixtures/protocol/test_protocol.py` implements independent format
oracles with Python `jsonschema.FormatChecker`. These are fixture checks, not a
new production validator.

The observation envelope is
`{ "protocolVersion": 1, "facts": [["nx_relation", [arguments]], ...] }`.
Mapping to F1 tables is identity: retain relation names, positional arguments
and values without renaming, coercion or defaults. Each observation carries
exactly one typed subject row through `nx_observation_options` or
`nx_observation_definitions`; text subject fields are removed. The link is
mandatory for every observation state and must remain in its request context and
target, as enforced by F1. The schema checks the envelope and string/array tuple
shape. Then the complete unordered fact collection **must** pass
`schema/abi.py`'s `validate`; envelope acceptance alone is insufficient. F1 owns
relation names, arity, types, identity framing, canonical encodings, references,
uniqueness and scope. Empty facts are representable but cannot serve as a
passing extraction oracle.

## States and exact metadata

Capabilities, phases, targets, request results, observations, syntax results and
diagnostics use their existing F1 relations and separate status vocabularies. A
discovery failure can precede any target. Partial metadata work can record
failed observations without manufacturing a successful result. Missing facts
never imply false or completion.

`text-field-too-large` is an explicit refusal; an affected request cannot claim
completion. Priority transport preserves canonical signed decimal strings over
the F1 signed 64-bit domain, including negative priorities; unsupported range
uses `priority-domain-unsupported`. Native QL integers cannot substitute for
those strings.

These fixtures prove metadata representation and exact text only. They do not
prove authentic source admission, budget enforcement or atomic publication.

## Verification and changes

Run from the repository root in a Python environment containing `jsonschema`:

```bash
python packages/codeql-nix/checks/fixtures/protocol/test_protocol.py
```

The tests check required descriptors, nested source roots and input identities,
retained metadata facets, rejection of deferred controls, literal paths and
budgets, all 25 relation mappings, status families and pre-target failures,
priorities, and UTF-8/JSON-expansion boundaries. They use independent fixtures
and F1 validation without invoking Nix evaluation or the CodeQL engine. F3 must
integrate this standalone entry point into the owner's checks with nonempty
health/ABI sentinels; F2 adds no check registration.

Change the relevant schema and independent fixture expectations together,
preserve all three enabled format checks and the F1 validation layer, then
format changed files and rerun the standalone suite. Update F1 first for
relation or metadata-semantic changes rather than duplicating its validator
here. Update this note when the transport or validation obligations change;
future runtime acceptance must separately establish evaluator isolation and
source admission.
